source.title_on_document: Exploring the Application and Influence of Artificial Intelligence AIGC Technology on Logo Design

paper_design_summary: The paper describes an online questionnaire sampling 50 design professionals from school-enterprise cooperation enterprises and comparing AIGC-generated with manually designed logos. It reports aesthetics, innovation, and brand-expression ratings and qualitative feedback, but does not identify the sampled professionals as the creators of the evaluated logos or describe allocation to AI assistance. The stated random sampling concerns recruitment, not assignment to design conditions (PDF p. 5, printed p. 455, sections 3.1-3.2 and Table 1).

studies.label: Questionnaire comparison of AIGC-generated and manually designed logos

assignment.what_was_assigned: No allocation of people to AI assistance is described. The stated comparison is AIGC-generated versus manually designed logos; the quoted random sampling describes selection of questionnaire participants. Whether the same respondents rated both design methods is not stated.
assignment.quote: Sample selection: random sampling, participants are selected from design professionals in school-enterprise cooperation enterprises.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 455), section 3.1 items (3)-(4) and section 3.2 independent variable; no condition-assignment mechanism is given.

arms.name: AIGC-generated design
arms.description: Logos generated using AIGC. Table 1 reports a sample size of 50 for each score, but does not report the number of people producing these logos or assigned to this design method (PDF p. 5, printed p. 455, section 3.2 and Table 1).

arms.name: Manual design
arms.description: Manually designed logos, also called artificial design in the paper. Table 1 reports a sample size of 50 for each score, but does not report the number of people producing these logos or assigned to this design method (PDF p. 5, printed p. 455, section 3.2 and Table 1).

participants.who: Design professionals from school-enterprise cooperation enterprises; the online questionnaire is addressed to professional designers and relevant industry experts. The analyzed count denotes the stated questionnaire sample, supported by the sample sizes in Table 1; it is not a count of people assigned to create logos. Creator counts and distinct respondent counts by design method are not reported.
participants.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 455), section 3.1 items (3)-(4), section 3.2 and Table 1.

ai_tool.name_model: Stable-Diffusion, Dream Studio.ai and Prodia are illustrated; the tool or model used for the logos evaluated in Table 1 is not specified.
ai_tool.how_used: Section 2.3 illustrates automatic logo generation from a clothing-brand description using red and gold and Chinese elements, with possible manual customization. Section 3.2 compares AIGC-generated and manual logos without specifying the evaluated logos, model versions, prompts, or participant use of the tools (PDF pp. 2-5, printed pp. 452-455, section 2.3, Figures 1-3 and section 3.2).

task.description: Logo design: the illustrative brief requests a clothing-brand logo using red and gold and Chinese motifs. The empirical comparison rates AIGC-generated and manual logos on aesthetics, innovation and brand expression; the paper does not describe a logo-production task assigned to the questionnaire participants (PDF pp. 3-5, printed pp. 453-455, section 2.3 and sections 3.1-3.2).

outcomes.name: Innovation score (manual-design row labeled Creative Score)
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: AIGC: mean 7.110, SD 0.437; manual design: mean 8.550, SD 0.253. Table 1 lists Sample Size 50 for each design method; these are questionnaire score samples, not documented creator-arm counts. The scale ranges from 1 (Very unoriginal) to 10 (very innovative). No inferential test is reported.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 455), section 3.2 scale definition and Table 1, Creative Score Manual Design / Innovation Score AIGC rows; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 456), Innovation score paragraph.

contrasts.reported: AIGC: mean 8.770, SD 0.252; manual design: mean 7.600, SD 0.303. Table 1 lists Sample Size 50 for each design method. The scale ranges from 1 (very unaesthetic) to 10 (very aesthetic). No inferential test is reported.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 455), section 3.2 scale definition and Table 1, Aesthetics Score Artificial Design / Aesthetic score AIGC rows; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 456), Aesthetic score paragraph.

contrasts.reported: Table 1: AIGC mean 6.950, SD 0.171; manual design mean 8.750, SD 0.152; Sample Size 50 for each design method. The scale ranges from 1 (very inaccurate) to 10 (very accurate). The accompanying prose instead prints the manual-design SD as 0.253; this conflicts with Table 1. No inferential test is reported.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 455), section 3.2 scale definition and Table 1, Brand expression score artificial design / Brand Expression Score AIGC rows; conflicting SD in PDF p. 6 (printed p. 456), Brand Expression Score paragraph.

eligibility.reason: Core eligibility remains unclear because the paper does not report random assignment to AI assistance or the number of people producing the rated logos. The 50 design professionals are the online-questionnaire sample; random sampling describes their recruitment, and neither that respondent count nor the repeated Table 1 sample sizes establishes the core threshold of 50 creative-task participants (PDF p. 5, printed p. 455, section 3.1 items (3)-(4), section 3.2 and Table 1; creativity-codebook.md, section 3, criteria 1-2). The documented comparison is AIGC-generated versus manually designed outputs with ratings scored on the logos, supporting criterion 3 and ai_vs_human context (PDF p. 5, printed p. 455, section 3.2 and Table 1).

one_line_finding: AIGC-generated logos received lower innovation ratings than manually designed logos (mean 7.110, SD 0.437 versus mean 8.550, SD 0.253; PDF p. 5, printed p. 455, Table 1), but random assignment to AI assistance is not reported.

audit_corrections.basis: The empirical comparison rates AI-generated logos against manually designed logos; the 50 professionals are questionnaire raters, and no participant receives AI assistance.
